name: Florida
overview: Florida uses a two-stage system. Each county tax collector first sells tax certificates (liens) on delinquent real estate taxes, with bidders competing by bidding the interest rate down from a statutory maximum of 18 percent per year; the sale must be held on or before June 1 (or the 60th day after delinquency, whichever is later) and may be run electronically. If the taxes are not redeemed, a certificate holder may apply for a tax deed once two years have passed since April 1 of the year the certificate was issued. The property is then sold at a public tax deed auction conducted by the clerk of the circuit court (in some counties another designated office), which may be held online instead of by public outcry, with a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater.

counties.office: Clerk of the Court and Comptroller of Miami-Dade County
counties.next_sale_note: The Clerk posts tax deed sale dates on its online auction calendar, not on its own pages.
counties.how_to_bid: Bidders must first register on the official online Foreclosure & Tax Deed Sales site, then review properties and sale dates there.
